thread:
Sofia (CS): Quick heads-up — SilverLake reserved pool onboarding. Goal: shift 25% traffic to reserved GPUs on Tue 03:00 UTC. Need quota confirmation, autoscale policy, and a short loadtest window. @Jamal @Pavel @Maya

Maya (CS): SilverLake is committed for Q3 renewal but flagged a potential risk if warmup fails. They want 4x concurrency for embeddings and 2x for chat.

Jamal (SRE): Re quotas: current reserved pool shows 48 GPUs. After overhead we have approx 44 usable. Are they expecting steady 60 rps or spiky bursts?

Sofia (CS): They expect a steady baseline ~40 rps and bursts up to 180 rps for 10m every hour during business hours.

Pavel (Runtime): For chat model variants — are we serving quantized 4-bit for dedicated? If yes we should test sequence length = 1024 for worst-case KV cache.

Maya (CS): Client prefers the quantized profile to hit cost targets. Confirmed with them earlier.

Jamal (SRE): OK. Autoscale plan suggestion: min replicas to cover baseline (40 rps), scale up based on token-rate threshold + request queue depth. Can we pin target p99 latency < 450ms?

Sofia (CS): Yes p99 < 450ms is the SLA. Also want fallback route to hosted small model if dedicated degrades.

Pavel (Runtime): I propose prefix/KV caching enabled for the repetitive prompts and set batching window to 15ms. That should reduce tokens/sec pressure.

Maya (CS): Load test window request: Tue 02:00–03:30 UTC (warmup + soak + burst). Will need runbook steps and contact list.

Jamal (SRE): I can run the loadtest from our infra. Share the load script. Will monitor GPU util, queue depth, p99, and error rate.

Maya (CS): Load script snippet (locust):
```
from locust import HttpUser, task, between
class User(HttpUser):
    wait_time = between(0.01, 0.1)
    @task
    def chat(self):
        self.client.post('/v1/generate', json={"model":"silverlake-chat-q4","input":"Hello world"})
```

Sofia (CS): Thanks. @deploy-bot can you confirm we have the canary route and fallback configured for SilverLake? Link to runbook: https://playbook.redwood/silverlake/onboard

deploy-bot: Canary route configured: service/silverlake-dedicated -> weight 0.25; fallback route present: service/silverlake-hosted (weight 0.75). Last deploy: 2247998000.

Pavel (Runtime): I'll prepare the quantization variant on the reserved pool and run a short priming batch to fill KV caches before the soak. Expect ~12 minutes for priming to avoid cold-cache penalties.

Jamal (SRE): Do we have an autoscale policy TTL on scale-down? Recommend 3m to avoid thrashing with hourly bursts.

Sofia (CS): Agreed. 3m scale-down TTL. Also need CS/Sales enablement note for customer-facing comms in case we hit degradation. Maya will own communication.

Maya (CS): I'll draft the email template and sign-off flows. Also capturing feedback: SilverLake asked for per-route cost breakdown post-test.

Pavel (Runtime): Will export token/cost metrics and put into the dashboard after test.

Jamal (SRE): One more ask — please whitelist our loadgen IPs in SilverLake's firewall (they use a strict allowlist).

Maya (CS): Done — they confirmed in the portal.

Sofia (CS): Action items summary:
- Jamal: run loadtest Tue 02:00–03:30 UTC, monitor metrics, enforce 3m scale-down TTL
- Pavel: priming batch + enable prefix cache + prepare quantized variant
- Maya: customer comms + provide load script + confirm whitelist
- deploy-bot: validate canary + fallback at shift

Please reply with ✅ when complete so I can mark onboarding step green.

Jamal (SRE): ✅ starting smoke checks now.

Pavel (Runtime): ✅ priming job queued.

Maya (CS): ✅ comms sent to SilverLake CSM.

deploy-bot: Smoke deploy check: all services healthy (ok=23, degraded=0).

Sofia (CS): Awesome — will update the ticket and loop in account exec for renewal cadence. Thanks team :tada:
